title: DINOv3 · Global and local
question: Why can rising image-classification accuracy miss a dense-feature problem?
choices: CLS discrimination and patch coherence serve different needs.
Every patch must have the same vector.
Classification directly measures boundary accuracy.
Register tokens are annotation masks.
explanation: The report observes rising global accuracy alongside declining dense segmentation; patch similarity must also be checked.

title: DINOv3 · Masked targets
question: What does the iBOT branch predict?
choices: Raw RGB pixels only.
Teacher prototype distributions at student-masked patch positions.
Human segmentation masks.
The future Gram-teacher update time.
explanation: iBOT is latent-target reconstruction using an unmasked EMA-teacher view, not supervised mask prediction.

title: DINOv3 · Matrix dimensions
question: For P normalized patch vectors of width d, what is the patch Gram shape?
choices: d × d
P × d
P × P
One scalar per class
explanation: X has shape P × d; X Xᵀ compares every pair of patch positions, producing P × P.

title: DINOv3 · Coordinate freedom
question: Which change preserves a patch Gram matrix?
choices: Arbitrary independent changes to each patch.
Multiplying all features by 10 without normalization.
Deleting all patch positions.
The same orthogonal rotation applied to every patch vector.
explanation: A shared orthogonal Q obeys Q Qᵀ = I, so (XQ)(XQ)ᵀ = X Xᵀ.

title: DINOv3 · Loss arithmetic
question: If two symmetric Gram errors are each 0.6 and all others zero, what is the squared Frobenius loss?
explanation: Both off-diagonal entries count: 0.6² + 0.6² = 0.72. A mean reduction would have a different scale.

title: DINOv3 · Teacher clocks
question: How does the Gram teacher differ from the ordinary EMA teacher during refinement?
choices: Both receive supervised gradients.
Gram is fixed between discrete refreshes; EMA updates every step.
Gram updates every patch; EMA stays early forever.
They are two names for a single permanently identical model.
explanation: The Gram target begins at an early snapshot, then copies EMA every 10k steps, at most three updates in Appendix C.

title: DINOv3 · Frozen does not mean untrained
question: What does frozen-backbone linear probing still require?
choices: Updating the encoder on every target image.
Applying Gram loss at test time.
Training a prediction head with labeled downstream data.
A caption for every inference image.
explanation: The encoder is fixed, but the linear predictor and trained normalization use downstream supervision.

title: DINOv3 · Causal evidence
question: Why does the final DINOv3 versus DINOv2 table not isolate Gram anchoring?
choices: mIoU is always meaningless.
Both methods have identical data and architecture.
DINOv3 is evaluated only on its training labels.
Capacity, data and training recipe also differ.
explanation: The closer Figure 9 ablation varies anchoring settings; final-model comparisons change several factors at once.
